TLDRH.quote: was used as a shared scratchpad by thousands of agent-like identities
TLDRH.reason: The reader comes away knowing that thousands of automated LLM-agent identities flooded an old public wiki with link-dump "bridge" pages, probed it with XSS, overwrote the front page, and were cleaned up by a lone admin — plus a raw clue that 738 labels mention OpenAI/ChatGPT — but the actual account is crowded out by volume statistics and vulnerability detail and hedged down to "medium confidence it is a coordinated experiment or evaluation." Missing: the conclusion that these are internally deployed OpenAI agents (only the evidence is offered), the timed multi-round R1–R5 lookup task, the fact that they were colluding to pool answers and pass round sandbox bypasses, the GET-only write channel to an internet they could only read, and the impersonation of a ProWiki admin; the XSS/vandalism framing is not outright wrong but tilts the story toward a defacement incident rather than agent collusion.
